title: Add scripture notes to playlists and reading plans
summary: Scripture items in playlists and reading plans can now carry a note: an optional title plus formatted text. While the playlist plays, the note shows right next to the passage (a pop-up beside the verses on a computer, a sheet above the chapter buttons on a phone), and the passage stays highlighted while the note is open. The PR also fixes two bugs: a playlist didn't scroll to its first passage if you were already on that chapter, and saving a playlist could silently lose changes to an item you had open for editing. Reading plans also get a new pencil button to edit an existing reading.

setup.title: Open the preview on a computer
setup.body: Open the preview link above in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a computer, with the browser window maximized. A wide screen (a laptop or bigger) works best. If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload.

setup.title: Make sure you have the newest version
setup.body: The app saves a copy of itself in your browser, so it can show an older version. Do a hard refresh once: **Ctrl+Shift+R** on Windows, or **Cmd+Shift+R** on Mac. A private/incognito window gives you a clean start if anything looks odd.

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Sign in with your email address. You'll get a code by email, so use an inbox you can check. You need to be signed in to create playlists and reading plans.

setup.title: Know how to start a playlist
setup.body: Playlists are in the **Discover** pane. To play one, find it there and click its round **Play playlist** button (the ▶ triangle). If a playlist is already playing, stop it first with **Stop** in the bottom toolbar.

sections.title: Writing notes in the playlist editor
sections.intro: These tests build a playlist called **Notes test** that the playback tests use later, so do them in order.

setup.title: Start a new playlist
setup.body: Open the **Discover** pane, click **+ Create**, then **Playlist**. Type `Notes test` as the playlist title. Leave the editor open. Items are added under **Add item**, choosing the kind with the **Item type** dropdown.

tests.title: A scripture item can get a note with a title and formatted text
tests.why: This is the main new feature: the **Add a note** link on scripture items.
steps: Set **Item type** to **Scripture** and type `Matthew 5:3-6` in the reference box.
Click **Add a note** under the reference box.
In the **Title (optional)** box, type `The upside-down kingdom`.
Click into the note text box below it and type `Blessed are the poor in spirit.` Then select the word `poor` and make it bold (**Ctrl+B** on Windows, **Cmd+B** on Mac).
Click **Add item**.
expected: After clicking **Add a note**, a **Note** area appears with a **Title (optional)** box, a text box with formatting, and a **Remove note** link. The cursor is in the text box.
After adding, the item appears in the playlist's list as Matthew 5:3-6, with `The upside-down kingdom` shown under it and the note text below that, with **poor** in bold.
The **Add item** area is empty again, with the **Add a note** link back (the note area closed).

tests.title: A note can be just a title, or just text
tests.why: A title alone is meant to be a complete note.
steps: Set **Item type** to **Text**, type `Pause` as its title and `Take a breath before the next reading.` as its text, and click **Add item**.
Set **Item type** to **Scripture**, type `Psalm 23`, click **Add a note**, type `Listen for the shepherd` in **Title (optional)**, leave the text box empty, and click **Add item**.
Add another **Scripture** item: `John 1`. Click **Add a note**, leave the title empty, type `Read the whole chapter slowly.` in the text box, and click **Add item**.
expected: Psalm 23 appears in the list with `Listen for the shepherd` under it and no note text.
John 1 appears with `Read the whole chapter slowly.` under it and no title.
The Pause text item appears between Matthew 5:3-6 and Psalm 23.

tests.title: A passage that covers two chapters, and a passage with no note
tests.why: Sets up the playback tests for multi-chapter passages and passages without notes.
steps: Add a **Scripture** item `Romans 8-9` with a note: title `Paul's big turn`, text `Watch how chapter 8 leads into 9.`
Add a **Scripture** item `Mark 1:1` with **no** note (don't click **Add a note**).
Save the playlist with **Save** (or **Save & exit**).
expected: Both items appear in the list. Romans 8-9 shows its note title and text; Mark 1:1 shows only the reference.
The playlist saves without any warning, and **Notes test** shows up in Discover.
If the reference box won't accept `Romans 8-9`, mark this test **Blocked**, note it, and use `Romans 8` instead for later tests.

tests.title: Editing an item fills in its note, and Remove note drops it
tests.before: Uses the **Notes test** playlist. Open it in the editor again (its options menu, **Edit playlist**).
steps: In the playlist's list, open **Matthew 5:3-6** for editing (its **Edit item** button).
Look at the item's fields.
Click **Cancel** on the item without changing anything.
Open **Mark 1:1** for editing, click **Add a note**, type `Temporary` in the title, then click **Remove note**.
Click **Save changes** on the item.
expected: Matthew 5:3-6 opens with its reference filled in, and its note already open: title `The upside-down kingdom` and the text with **poor** in bold.
Cancel closes the item with no question asked, and nothing changes.
After **Remove note**, the note area closes and **Add a note** is back. Mark 1:1 is saved with no note: the list shows only its reference.

tests.title: Saving the playlist with an item open asks before losing your changes
tests.why: Bug fix. Before, changes to an item you had open for editing were silently lost when you saved the playlist.
steps: Still in the **Notes test** editor, open **Psalm 23** for editing.
Change its note title to `Listen for the good shepherd`, but don't click **Save changes** on the item.
Click the playlist's **Save** button.
In the question that appears, click **Back**.
Click the playlist's **Save** again, and this time click **Keep changes and save**.
expected: A question titled **Unsaved item changes** appears: "You've changed an item but haven't saved those changes yet. What would you like to do?" with **Back**, **Discard and save** and **Keep changes and save**.
**Back** closes the question and leaves you in the editor with your typed change still there.
**Keep changes and save** saves the playlist. Opening the editor again shows Psalm 23 with the title `Listen for the good shepherd`.

tests.title: Discard and save keeps the item as it was
steps: Open **Notes test** in the editor again and open **Psalm 23** for editing.
Change its note title to `Should not be saved`.
Click the playlist's **Save**, then click **Discard and save**.
Open the editor again and look at Psalm 23.
expected: The playlist saves.
Psalm 23 still has the title `Listen for the good shepherd`, not `Should not be saved`.

tests.title: Opening an item and saving without changes doesn't ask anything
tests.why: Before, an item opened for editing always counted as changed, so you'd be asked even when nothing had been touched.
steps: In the **Notes test** editor, open **John 1** for editing. Don't change anything.
Click the playlist's **Save**.
expected: The playlist saves straight away, with no **Unsaved item changes** question.

sections.title: Notes during playback on a computer
sections.intro: Keep the browser window wide (maximized) unless a test says otherwise. Each test continues from the one before it while **Notes test** keeps playing.

tests.title: A note pops up beside the passage it's about
steps: Play **Notes test**.
Look at the reader and the pop-up that appears.
expected: The reader goes to Matthew 5 and scrolls to verses 3-6. Those verses are highlighted and the rest of the chapter is dimmed.
A pop-up appears in the empty space to the **right** of the text, level with verses 3-6, with a small pointer toward them.
At the top of the pop-up is a small line `Matthew 5:3-6`, and under it the title `The upside-down kingdom` in larger text. Below is the note text with **poor** in bold.

The pop-up has **Previous** / **Next** buttons, a count like `1 of 7`, and an **X** to close it. It has a visible border, and there's no dark overlay over the rest of the page: you can still scroll and select verses.

tests.title: The passage stays highlighted while the note is open, and fades after closing it
steps: With the Matthew 5 note open, wait about 10 seconds.
Click the **X** on the note.
Watch the highlighted verses for a few seconds.
Click **Show note**.
expected: After 10 seconds the verses are still highlighted (before this change, the highlight always faded after about 3 seconds).
After the **X**, the note closes and a **Show note** button appears. About 1.5 seconds later the highlight fades and the chapter is no longer dimmed.
**Show note** brings the note back, and verses 3-6 are highlighted again.

tests.title: The note moves under the passage when there's no room beside the text
steps: Make the browser window narrower step by step (drag its edge) until there's no empty space beside the chapter text. Stop before it switches to the phone layout.
Then make the window wide again.
expected: When there's no room beside the text, the note moves to just **below** verses 3-6, still pointing at them. A long note scrolls inside the pop-up instead of running off the screen.
When the window is wide again, the note moves back to the right of the text.

tests.title: A note waits in the corner when its passage is scrolled away
steps: Scroll the reader down until verses 3-6 are off the screen.
Scroll back up.
expected: With the verses off screen, the note sits in a corner of the reading area, without a pointer.
Scrolling back puts it beside the verses again.

tests.title: Moving to a non-scripture step clears the highlight right away
steps: Click **Next** on the note.
expected: The **Pause** text item opens the way text items always have.
The Matthew 5 highlight and dimming disappear immediately, without waiting.

tests.title: A title-only note is headed by its title
steps: Move on to the next step (**Next**).
expected: The reader goes to Psalm 23 and the note appears beside it.
The note shows a small `Psalm 23` line and the title `Listen for the good shepherd`, with no text below it.
The passage stays highlighted while the note is open.

tests.title: A whole-chapter note with no title is headed by the passage
steps: Click **Next** on the note to reach **John 1**.
expected: The note is headed by the passage (`John 1`) with no separate title, and shows `Read the whole chapter slowly.`
It points at the chapter heading at the top of John 1, rather than at particular verses.

tests.title: A passage spanning two chapters shows its note on the first chapter only
steps: Click **Next** to reach **Romans 8**.
Click **Next** again to reach **Romans 9**.
expected: On Romans 8 the note `Paul's big turn` appears.
On Romans 9 there's no note. The note isn't repeated on the second chapter.

tests.title: A passage without a note still fades its highlight after about 3 seconds
steps: Move on to **Mark 1:1** (the last step).
Watch the highlighted verse for about 5 seconds.
expected: No note pop-up appears.
Mark 1:1 is highlighted at first, and the highlight fades after about 3 seconds, the same as before this PR.

tests.title: The queue shows the note's title after the reference
steps: While **Notes test** is still playing, look at the **Queue** section in the Discover pane.
expected: Matthew 5:3-6 is listed as `Matthew 5:3-6 · The upside-down kingdom`, with the title in a lighter weight.
Psalm 23 shows `· Listen for the good shepherd` the same way. John 1 and Mark 1:1 show only the reference.

tests.title: The note looks right in dark mode
steps: Stop the playlist, switch the app to the dark theme in **Settings**, and play **Notes test** again.
expected: The note pop-up is readable and has a visible outline, so it doesn't blend into the dark page.
The highlighted verses are still easy to tell apart from the dimmed ones.

tests.title: For a right-to-left translation the note sits on the left
tests.why: Optional: skip this if you can't find a right-to-left translation.
steps: Stop the playlist and switch the Bible translation to a right-to-left one (for example an Arabic or Hebrew translation).
Play **Notes test** again with the window wide.
expected: The Matthew 5 note appears in the empty space to the **left** of the text, pointing at verses 3-6.

sections.title: Notes during playback on a phone

setup.title: Use a phone-width screen
setup.body: Use a phone and sign in there, or make your computer's browser window very narrow (about the width of a phone) so the app switches to its phone layout. Stop any playlist that's playing.

tests.title: The note sits above the chapter buttons without covering them
steps: Play **Notes test**.
Look at the bottom of the screen.
expected: A note sheet sits directly above the floating chapter navigation at the bottom, showing `Matthew 5:3-6`, the title `The upside-down kingdom` and the note text.
The chapter's previous/next buttons are still fully visible and can be tapped.

tests.title: Tapping the note's heading collapses it, and the next note opens again
steps: Tap the note sheet's heading (where the title is).
Tap it again to open it.
Tap it once more to collapse it, then move on through the steps until you reach **Psalm 23**.
expected: The sheet collapses to one line, and the Matthew 5 highlight fades about 1.5 seconds later. Opening it again brings the highlight back.
On Psalm 23 the sheet is open again by itself.
Psalm 23's note has only a title, so its heading doesn't collapse when tapped (there's nothing to hide).

tests.title: The end of the chapter can always be scrolled above the note
tests.why: Before, the sheet could hide the last verses of the chapter.
steps: Go back to the **Matthew 5:3-6** step with its note open.
Scroll all the way to the bottom of Matthew 5.
Collapse the note and scroll to the bottom again.
expected: With the note open, the last verse (verse 48) can be scrolled fully above the note sheet. Nothing at the end of the chapter is stuck underneath it.
With the note collapsed, the empty space at the bottom shrinks to match, so there isn't a large blank gap.

sections.title: Playlists scroll to their first passage

tests.title: Starting a playlist on the chapter you're already reading scrolls to its passage
tests.why: Bug fix. Before, starting a playlist at Matthew 5:20 while already reading Matthew 5 did nothing: no scroll and no highlight.
tests.before: Use a computer with the window wide.
steps: Create a playlist called `Scroll test` with one **Scripture** item, `Matthew 5:20`, and save it.
Open **Matthew 5** in the reader and scroll to the very top, so verse 20 is off the screen.
Play **Scroll test**.
expected: The reader scrolls down to Matthew 5:20 and highlights it.

sections.title: Notes in reading plans
sections.intro: These tests build a reading plan called **Notes plan**, so do them in order.

setup.title: Create a plan with one reading
setup.body: Open **Reading plans** and click **Create reading plan**. Name it `Notes plan` and continue to **Select readings**. In **Session 1**, add a **Scripture** reading `Psalm 1` with **no** note. Finish with **Create plan**.

tests.title: An existing reading can be edited to add a note
tests.why: New: before, readings could only be added or removed, so there was no way to add a note to a reading already in a plan.
steps: Open **Notes plan** and choose **Edit plan** (in its **Plan options** menu).
Go to the readings step. Next to **Psalm 1**, click the new pencil button (**Edit reading**).
Click **Add a note**, type `Two paths` as the title and `Notice the two ways this psalm describes.` as the text.
Click **Save changes** on the reading, then **Save changes** for the plan.
expected: The pencil button opens Psalm 1 in the reading box, with `Psalm 1` filled in.
After saving the reading, the plan's reading list shows Psalm 1 with a one-line excerpt under it: `Two paths · Notice the two ways this psalm describes.`
The plan saves without any warning.

tests.title: Saving a plan with a reading open asks before losing your changes
steps: Choose **Edit plan** on **Notes plan** again, and click **Edit reading** on Psalm 1.
Change the note title to `Two ways`, but don't click **Save changes** on the reading.
Click **Save changes** for the plan, then choose **Keep changes and save**.
expected: The **Unsaved item changes** question appears, with **Back**, **Discard and save** and **Keep changes and save**.
After **Keep changes and save**, the plan saves and Psalm 1's excerpt now starts with `Two ways`.

tests.title: A reading plan's note shows while reading
steps: Open **Notes plan**, choose **Start plan** (pick any pace), and click **Read** on the first day or session.
expected: The reader opens Psalm 1 with the passage highlighted.
The note appears beside it (or above the chapter buttons on a phone), headed by `Psalm 1` and the title `Two ways`, with the note text below.

notCovered: The AI playlist tools reading and keeping notes. This is covered by automated tests; if you use the AI to edit **Notes test**, check that its notes are still there afterwards.
Cleaning unsafe content out of note text (for example scripts pasted into a note). This is covered by automated tests.
Progress already recorded in a reading plan staying in place after editing a reading. This is covered by automated tests.
The larger server bundle mentioned in the PR description. That's a build-size question for reviewers, not something visible in the app.
